Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with a wrist fracture. The reported mechanism is consistent with the
type and force of the injury sustained. Initial imaging and reduction were completed, and the patient was placed in
immobilization with follow-up scheduled as is standard for this fracture pattern. Over the course of 16 visits, treatment ran
somewhat longer than is typical for an injury of this kind, with progressive rehabilitation including range-of-motion exercises,
grip strengthening, and monitoring of healing. Several examination findings, including tenderness over the fracture site and
reduced grip strength, support the diagnosis, while other neurovascular and sensory testing returned within normal limits. No
prior injury to the same area is known from the patient history. Billing records were reviewed and show no duplicate or repeated
charges for the same services. Ongoing care is directed toward full functional recovery, with a plan for reassessment at the next
scheduled visit.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
